summary: The SwiftUI shell: the sky and theme, components, navigation, sign-in, the agreement, legal pages, accounts and settings.

src/App.jsx.note: The app's states (the legal pages, restoring with "Signing you in…" while a sign-in that came back is finished, a sign-in that came back without a session, the agreement screen and its checking line, the front page, the shell, remade per account), useProfile, and the providers above and below the per-account identity: the composer's (ComposerHost, held by AppRoot above the account, whose ToastCenter is the app's one, App.jsx's ToastProvider, the shell's toasts and the composer's in one column; Composer/ComposerHost.swift, ComposerContext.jsx's entry), the archive's (ArchiveHost, one ArchiveModel per signed-in account, its store in the app's file store, its handle the profile's once the profile is that account's, else the remembered one's; deleting an account's data deletes its archive and starts every store handle afresh) and the dashboards' (ShellDashboards, made by ShellView per account). A compose link opened while signed out is kept in the tab store for after the sign-in (PendingCompose) and the front page says so. An account switched to in place is decided for the agreement afresh in the same pass, from its stored note, so nothing of it is drawn on the last account's answer. A Defense scan goes when its account is signed out or forgotten (ScanStore's keepScansFor over the accounts not needing a sign-in), and the shell is made again when the number and date formats change (`.id(preferences.formats)`, the web's `<Shell key={formats}>`; the dashboards are read again from the store, which every change is written to at once). On iOS a sign-in comes back into the running app, so a failed one is the session's error on whatever page is up.

src/accounts/AccountMenu.jsx.note: All of it, with the compact menu's Sync now once there is an archive to sync. A native Menu: an account's row carries a person glyph, since a native menu item can't show the picture. The pending-work read before a long session's sign-out (useSignOutGuard, and Sign out of all's usePendingWork) goes through AppModel.pendingWork, VirgaPosting's listScheduled and listTimers over the account's VirgaBackend (PendingWorkServices.posting, VirgaPosting/Wiring.swift); a read that fails says it couldn't check, as the web's does.

src/accounts/AccountsSettings.jsx.note: All of it; the pending-work warnings in Remove … from this browser read through AppModel.pendingWork (VirgaPosting's listScheduled and listTimers, PendingWorkServices.posting). Refocusing the next row's ⋯ after a removal is the system's.

src/accounts/SessionNotices.jsx.note: The hand-off before a sign-in again (with Cancel), the stuck account's button and the sign-in's notices. Deliberately not: 'another tab switched accounts', since every window of the app shares one session (AppModel).

src/accounts/accounts.css.note: The rows of Settings › Account, the front page's remembered accounts and the session notices. The account menu's list styles are the native Menu's on iOS.

src/charts/charts.css.note: The chart tokens (--chart-1/2, --chart-area, --chart-grid, --chart-ghost, --heat-0 to 6, --second-tip), the series chart's strokes, dashes, dots and marks, the tooltip's own grounds, the table view (TableScroll: at least the column or 28rem, whichever is less, at the column's start, its head held over the rows as they scroll, as `thead th { position: sticky }` has it, and straight under the chart foot's 44-point line on touch; a row's head in --ink-2), the bar list, the heatmap and the sparkline. Not as the web: the plot's margins and the rules' numbers are Swift Charts' own layout, and the widget's hidden marks list (.widget .an-chart-marks) waits for the dashboards.

src/components/Dialog.jsx.note: DialogFrame and .virgaDialog (a sheet): the title, Close, the content, the foot in equal halves on a phone; `stackActions` (.dialog--stack-actions: one under the other, the confirm first) and `autofocus: true` with `.dialogAutofocus()` on the field ([data-autofocus]: the dialog's own focus, inside its sheet, set when it opens). src/hillside/Hillside.jsx.note: HillsideView(phase:day:active:intro:depth:soft:crest:blur:): the flat picture under the canvas until the first picture is up (and for good with no Metal device or shaders that don't compile, the reason logged after "[Virga hillside]"), the canvas a bleed past each edge, fading in, then out of focus by blur when soft; --crest is `crest`, in points from the top, and --hill-blur is `blur`. The box against the window is IntersectionObserver's in view; the canvas's scene being active is the page's visibility. One deliberate difference: Hillside.jsx starts a scene the page has covered when the page is idle; here every scene starts once the GPU, made off the main thread, is ready.

src/hillside/LiveSky.jsx.note: The band, as tall as the wash (--sky-end), over the top of the wash wherever the wash is drawn (PageSky on every page of the shell, and the front page's sky), moved with it as the page scrolls, in PreferencesModel's effective sky, at depth 0.55 and never soft, and nothing in high contrast. Every page's band draws from one scene (LiveSkyDrivers), as the shell keeps one LiveSky while its pages change.

src/hillside/clouds.js.note: mulberry (HillsideRandom), makeNoise's bytes (uploaded as one channel of a mipmapped texture, since r, g and b are the same), the cloud kinds (TYPES), the cumulus, stratus and cirrus generators (GEN), makeCloud, measureTop and the fair day's layout (read from clouds.js's own source by the generator, since it doesn't export them), createClouds' batch with its drift round the back, its staging in Float32 and its stable back-to-front sort (HillsideCloudBatch, with Math.hypot as V8 works it out), and puffMaterial in Metal (HillsideShaders' hill_puff_*), instanced from a buffer of sixteen floats a puff.

src/hillside/hillside.css.note: The four flat pictures (laid out as a browser lays a gradient out: HillsideStyle.flatGradient), the crest, the canvas's bleed, its fade and its focus (still with Reduce Motion), and the live sky's band: the scene 1,100 tall with its crest at 96%, its filter (grayscale, brightness, contrast, each step clamped, in sRGB), its opacity (0.45 at night), its mask and its screen blend, which are the band's own pass in the shaders, drawing the wash too, so the band comes out opaque. iOS's own: on a phone's front page of a part, the strip held over the status bar is clear at rest over the live sky and comes in as the page scrolls under it (LiveSky.stripFade), since the web has no status bar.

src/hillside/land.js.note: height and createLand's mesh (uploaded with its positions and normals interleaved and 16-bit indices, as it has 60,800 vertices), and the land's ShaderMaterial in Metal (HillsideShaders' hill_land_*). The mesh is made, off the main thread, only for a hill's view: the live sky's band never reaches the hill.

src/hillside/scene.js.note: PALETTES, phaseOf, TURN, COLOR_KEYS and the helpers (HillsideScene, read from scene.js's own source by the generator, since it exports only createHillside), and createHillside's closure as HillsideSceneState: the light turning from one sky to another (the sun the short way round), aim and place (the crest where the page wants it, the intro, the pointer's lean and the sway), the wind, the clouds' update, and the frame loop (30 pictures a second unless the view is on the move, a turn under way finished out of view, nothing while hidden, the pace check lowering the pixel ratio, Reduce Motion's still pictures), held step by step to the web's own createHillside run over a recording stand-in for WebGL and requestAnimationFrame (hillside.scene); the sky's dome (SphereGeometry(30000, 48, 24)) and three.js's sums in HillsideMath. The sky's ShaderMaterial is Metal (HillsideShaders, compiled at run time), drawn by VirgaUI/Sky (HillsideRenderer; HillsideDriver is requestAnimationFrame, a display link at 30 or 60 a second, the visibility, an active scene's, and the pointer, a hovering one only: an iPad's trackpad or mouse, never a finger or a pencil). WebGL's context loss has no Metal counterpart: HillsideSceneState keeps contextLost for the cases, and nothing on iOS calls it. antialias is off, as the web has it at 2 pixels a point and more, which every iOS screen is.

VoiceOver hears the live regions' words as announcements ("Looking you up…", "Found {name}, {meta}.", a notice as it comes up, "Still here?"), and focus goes where the web sends it (the field, the way on while the account is looked up and found, else the card's title). The compose link's callout shows while one waits for the sign-in (AppRoot's \.signInComposing). On iOS the trip is ASWebAuthenticationSession: going again calls the one under way off and waits for it first, and closing Add an account calls the trip off with its sheet (not once the sign-in has come back and is being finished, which takes the page down itself).

src/styles/app.css.note: a few of its measures (the landing page's bar, title, lede and points, the return screen's title, the restoring message and its animation) are in ThemeKit (VirgaCore/Theme, from ios/parity/cases/_themeKit.js); it sets no theme tokens. The pages are VirgaUI's: the front page, its hero, points, foot and sketch (Pages/LandingView.swift), the narrow column and the restoring line (Pages/SignInReturnView.swift), with the measures ThemeKit doesn't read named in Theme/Measures.swift until _themeKit.js reads them; the live sky under the front page's content (.landing > :not(.live-sky)) is LandingFrame's sky, skyBackground(live:)

src/styles/base.css.note: the page's type (body size, line height, numerals, headings, links, code), focus outline, selection and the sky's wash are measures in ThemeKit (VirgaCore/Theme); it sets no theme tokens. VirgaUI draws them: the type in Instrument Sans with tabular figures, the body's 1.45 between lines unless a text says otherwise (headings 1.25) and, where a single line's box lays it out, the half-leading above and below (Theme/Typography.swift), the sky from the window's top behind the page, moved by its scroll, and once behind the sidebar and the page together beside the sidebar (Theme/SkyWash.swift), the focus outline, on the control it is put on (Components/Focus.swift), a Segmented key's inside it from 2 in out to the edge, Reduce Motion (Theme/Motion.swift). The element resets, ::selection and the helper classes (.visually-hidden, .skip-link) have no counterpart on iOS

src/styles/controls.css.note: 246 of its declarations, the kit's measures, are in ThemeKit (VirgaCore/Theme, listed in ios/parity/cases/_themeKit.js); the measures it doesn't read yet (the touch block's reaches, the line-heights of .btn, .segmented-key, .link-action and .token, a few of the table's and the select's) are in Theme/Measures.swift. The components are VirgaUI's (Components/): the button's tiers and sizes, the link action (its 1-point line at a 3-point offset, 2 while open or pressed) and the more link, Segmented and the sideways row (scrolled only far enough to clear its fade), the section and its head (the title's column beside the tools, and on a phone the small Segmented on a row of its own), foot (a ghost first let out to the edge) and caption, figures (the cells sharing their rows, the number at line height 1) and the delta, the figure note's faint dot (FigureNote), the menu (native, its icons in --ink-2), fields and the text area, the placeholder in --muted (VirgaTextField), select.input (VirgaSelect), the check (16, the terms page's 18 apart), the radio and the choice (Dialog.swift), the switch, badges, the meta line (the dot 6 after its word), chips, tokens, avatars, the dot, the table (a row read as one, with its heads), the empty state (16 under a flush head), the note, the callout, the disclosure (its arrow drawn and not read), progress, the info tip, and the touch block's sizes. The chart foot is Charts/ChartTable.swift's ShowAsTable and the list toolbar Tools/ArchiveSearchTool.swift's; the transitions are Theme/Motion.swift's. Not yet: .meta-group and .meta > .meta (ThemeKit.metaGroupGap is unread); .has-corner-menu (a phone row's ⋯ in its top corner; VirgaRow has no callers yet); the posting pages' fields, selects and danger callouts, still to move onto VirgaTextField, VirgaSelect and Callout(tone: .danger, words); and in Settings › Posting, the time zone (scheduleParts' TimezoneSelect, a menu Picker) and the composer's pickers it shows (LanguagePicker's and GatesEditor's fields). The chart foot's touch rules (44-point link actions, no gap between wrapped lines, a phone's ⋯ at the line's end) are ShowAsTable's (Charts/ChartTable.swift); every other field is VirgaTextField and every other select.input VirgaSelect (Settings, Settings › Posting's own cards and the timer's rule editor, the card settings, Defense); the dashboards' .stat-note, a dot after each of several parts, is FigureNote(deltaText:parts:) (Dashboards/Widgets.swift), as a figure's note is FigureNote

src/styles/theme.css.note: every token it sets on <html> and the cascade that picks them, in VirgaCore/Theme, resolved at a window's root and read as @Environment(\.virgaTheme) (Theme/VirgaTheme.swift). Its high-contrast rules for components are drawn in VirgaUI: the focus outline (Components/Focus.swift), a pressed key's line (Components/Segmented.swift), the switch, its knob at 70% (Components/Switch.swift), the narrow tab bar's disc's ring (Shell/MobileNav.swift); not yet heat cells and bar tracks (the charts), the current page's underline and the image labels. Its forced-colours rules are recorded but never apply: no device the app runs on has them.

src/tools/tools.css.note: Measure.Tools names every measure the tool pages use (the list of tools, the statement, the filter figures, the line over a table, the inline select, the activity check, the large search, the unfollow log's groups, the queue's ✕, the best slots, identity, the facts and the timeline, the lookup's field, its suggestions floating over the page, pair counts, legend, totals and events), and dashboards.css's person and post rows as the tools list them; each view draws its rules from them. The cleanup and lists tables are tables from 641 wide (the tick box's 36, the cleanup table's account at 36% of the table and the lists table's name taking what the rest leave, their words ending in an ellipsis, a ticked row's tint 10 past the sides, a row's own Unfollow stepping back while rows are ticked) and set as the web's phone sets them narrower. The hover rules are the pointer's on an iPad: a suggestion under the pointer becomes the active one; a name's underline on hover is left to the system's pointer effect.
